result.instructions: Drives the BEAM screen-reader mod for BeamNG.drive. Call `health` first -- it says whether a world is live and whether the game console answers. Every tool returns a clear error rather than hanging when the game is not running. `lua_exec` is the universal surface; `speech_log` is how you assert on what the mod announced; `speak` is how you give the user instructions mid-test.

tools.description: Whether the game and the mod are reachable: live world, telemetry age, console round-trip, uptime. Call this first in any session; every other tool's failure message points back here.
tools.name: health

tools.description: Execute Lua (or TorqueScript / UI JavaScript) inside BeamNG and return the value plus captured print output. context: 'ge' (Game Engine Lua, the only one that returns a value synchronously), 'ts', 'ui', 'veh:current' or 'veh:<id>' for a vehicle VM. This is the universal surface -- it reaches every mod diagnostic, including those with no UDP command.

code.description: Lua source. Use 'return ...' to get a value.

suppress_gui.description: Keep the result out of beamtel's console pane and out of the user's ears. Default true.

timeout_s.description: Default 5s for ge, 15s for a vehicle context.

tools.name: lua_exec

tools.description: List the execution contexts consoleAccessible offers, including one per loaded vehicle.
tools.name: lua_contexts

tools.description: Snapshot of beamtel's live state. Sections: telemetry, position, implement, trailer, dock, cannon, scanner, modes, slots, assistant, road, liveness. Omit `sections` for all.
tools.name: get_state

tools.description: The user's current beamtel configuration. Read-only by design -- the agent must not silently rewrite the user's settings. API keys and other secrets read back as `<redacted>` when set and empty when unset.
tools.name: get_config

tools.description: Observe the driving assistant while the player drives. start records vehicle inputs, AI steering/braking, route and turn choices at 5 Hz plus announcements and disengagement reasons to NDJSON. It does not enable or drive the assistant. status gives latest state and sample age; read returns events after since_seq; mark adds a note; stop closes the recording; review summarizes a session; list returns saved session names.
tools.name: assistant_diagnostic

tools.description: Record and review a road-guidance driving attempt. `start` opens a durable NDJSON session and enables detailed Lua lane-correction fields; `stop` closes it and returns an analysis of settled-band occupancy, correction episodes, rapid settled-tone retriggers, steering/target oscillation, and wheel slip. `status`, `list`, and `review` are read-only; `mark` adds a timestamped note.

action.description: start | stop | status | mark | review | list

note.description: mark: note about an observed event

session.description: review: bare .ndjson session file name; omit for latest

tools.name: road_diagnostic

tools.description: What the mod actually announced, as a sequence-numbered ring buffer. This is the assertion primitive: it records every say() call including the ones excluded from the user's replay buffer, and records calls that were suppressed during loading (spoken=false). Use `since_seq` as a cursor.

since_seq.description: Return only entries after this sequence number.

source.description: Filter by the say() source tag.

tools.name: speech_log

tools.description: Say something to the user through the mod's own speech output -- how to give instructions mid-test.
tools.name: speak

tools.description: Every F9 command the mod offers, with its modifiers and description. Works with no game running.
tools.name: list_commands

tools.description: Trigger an F9 command in-process (no OS key injection, no window focus needed) and return the speech it produced. One round trip is act plus assert. Note that some commands open modal UI.

name.description: The key pressed after F9, e.g. 's' for speed.

settle_ms.description: How long to wait for speech before reading it back.

tools.name: press_command

tools.description: Send a raw UDP command to one of the mod's Lua extensions. Fire-and-forget: verify the effect with get_state / speech_log / diag. Modules: beamtelAI, cameraInfo, clickspot, console, implementProximity, nodeGrabber, obstacleDetector, roadDetector, terrainScanner, uiToggle, vehicleBindings, vehicleScanner, vehicleSlots, vehicleSpawner

module.description: Extension name from the list above.

port.description: Escape hatch for a port not in the map.

tools.name: send_command

tools.description: Spawn, teleport, remove or reload vehicles -- how to build known test geometry. Teleport offsets are in FEET, rotations in degrees.

action.description: list_active | player_id | spawn | teleport | remove | reload | ignition_off

tools.name: vehicle_control

tools.description: Run one of the mod's Lua ground-truth diagnostics. Names: cannon, dock, implement_frame, implement_points, mouth_frame, player_id, ramp, ramp_retry, ramp_state_of, ramp_states, scanner_target, terrain, trailer. These print what the resolver actually chose, which is the only way to catch a confident wrong number.

veh_id.description: For the diagnostics that take a vehicle id.

tools.name: diag

tools.description: Turn the game's Lua log stream on or off, and read what it captured. Log records still reach beamtel's own console pane.
tools.name: console_log

tools.description: Move the eye. Switches camera mode (including free camera) and places the free camera anywhere, then returns the resulting camera state -- so a set is self-verifying in one round trip and pairs directly with `screenshot`. actions: get (default) | list_modes | set_mode | cycle | reset | place. `place` takes exactly one position form -- absolute (x/y/z), relative to a vehicle's own frame (rel_fwd_m/rel_right_m/rel_up_m), or orbit around one (orbit_distance_m + orbit_azimuth_deg/orbit_elevation_deg) -- plus an optional `look_at` that derives the orientation for you. Angles are in the mod's own convention: yaw 0-360 matching the 4450 feed and the Alt+H readout, pitch positive-UP. This never moves the vehicle.

action.description: get | list_modes | set_mode | cycle | reset | place

look_at.description: place: a [x, y, z] point or a vehicle id to aim at. Overrides yaw_deg/pitch_deg.

mode.description: set_mode: a camera name from list_modes, e.g. 'free', 'orbit', 'onboard.driver'.

offset.description: cycle: +1 for the next vehicle camera, -1 for the previous.

orbit_azimuth_deg.description: place, orbit: 0 puts the camera directly ahead of the vehicle, positive swings to its right.

orbit_distance_m.description: place, orbit: radius from the vehicle. Implies looking at it.

orbit_elevation_deg.description: place, orbit: degrees above the world horizontal.

pitch_deg.description: place: positive is looking UP, matching cameraInfo.lua.

rel_fwd_m.description: place, relative: metres along the vehicle's forward. Negative is behind it.

rel_right_m.description: place, relative: metres to the vehicle's RIGHT. Note this is a placement offset, so it is the mirror of the mod's positive-is-LEFT bearing convention.

rel_up_m.description: place, relative: metres along the vehicle's up.

settle_ms.description: Wait before reading the pose back.

veh_id.description: place: the vehicle a relative or orbit placement is measured against. Defaults to the player's.

yaw_deg.description: place: heading, 0-360, same convention as the 4450 camera feed.

tools.name: camera_control

tools.description: Capture the game and WRITE THE PNG TO A FILE for you to read -- the same capture path the AI Describer uses, with nothing sent to any model. Use it when a picture settles a question the numbers cannot: whether a car really is where a resolver says it is, what a mouth or an implement is actually pointing at, or what the mod's own UI is showing. Pass `dir` to put the file in your own working directory, then read that path. Pairs with `camera_control`: place the eye, then shoot.

dir.description: Directory to write into. Defaults to %LOCALAPPDATA%/beamtel/screenshots.

filename.description: Bare file name, no path. Defaults to a millisecond-stamped name so successive shots never collide.

focus_game.description: Raise the BeamNG window before the grab and put the previous window back afterwards. Needed whenever the game is minimized, which it usually is when an agent is driving -- a minimized BeamNG renders nothing and a plain grab returns the desktop. The result reports what was actually captured.

hide_ui.description: Hide the game HUD around the grab for a clean view of the world. Pass false to inspect the UI itself.

settle_ms.description: How long to let the game render a UI-free frame after hiding.

tools.name: screenshot

tools.description: Drop the mod's cached geometry (implement rebuild + ramp resolve re-arm) so the next test starts clean.
tools.name: reset_test_state
